28905-the-works-of-edward-bulwer-lytton-:
David Widger edited this linked index to the Project Gutenberg editions of Edward Bulwer-Lytton's works. Bulwer-Lytton, who lived from 1803 to 1873, wrote Athens: Its Rise and Fall, The Caxtons, Zicci, Eugene Aram, Pelham, Devereux, Ernest Maltrevers, and Kenelm Chillingly. His novels also include Harold, Lucretia, A Strange Story, The Last Days of Pompeii, and The Coming Race.

The index lists every volume and chapter, from My Novel and The Last of the Barons to Paul Clifford, Rienzi, Zanoni, and The Lady of Lyons. It lets a reader plan a path through a very large shelf, novel by novel. Bulwer-Lytton was once among England's most popular novelists, and this index helps modern readers find their way back to his romances, histories, and tales of the strange.
doe-osti-3019723-akiachak-energy-efficie:
Georgina Davis and Caitlynn Hanna of the National Laboratory of the Rockies reported the Akiachak Energy Efficiency Retrofit Project in NREL/TP-5600-96448, issued February 2026. Akiachak is a Yup'ik community in western Alaska, where heating oil and electricity costs bite hard. The project retrofitted community buildings for efficiency. Staff began with data: utility bills for electricity and number 1 heating oil were collected for buildings such as the Office building. Records were stored, then analyzed for changes in building performance and consumption.

Methods and results sections track energy use intensity across the retrofit. The report structure follows the work: background, objectives, activities, methods, then results. Rural Alaska retrofits live or die on logistics, since every material arrives by barge or air. Documenting one village's project in this detail gives the next village a template. Funders also gain an account of what the retrofit bought, in energy terms, building by building.
